title: Entrance facade showing Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, Faculty of Engineering
objects_and_counts: At least seven human figures or representations are visible: (1) a silhouetted pedestrian far left in the corridor, (2) a darker silhouette closer to the left foreground on the walkway, (3) a white mannequin or human-form figure standing inside near the main entrance, (4) a second white mannequin or human-form figure further inside to the left, (5) a silhouette of a person shown walking through the interior doorway to the right of the main entrance, (6) a shadowed silhouette of a person walking on the right background along the balustrade, and (7) a large foreground shadowed silhouette carrying a briefcase on the plaza. Some of these are ghosted silhouettes and all are visually distinct from printed images on posters or screens.

Four vertically oriented perforated metal/cladding panels are visible on the front elevation near the entrance (two at the corner and two flanking the glass entrance area); these panels are partially cropped by the image edges in places.
At least one freestanding red rectangular/cube object is visible immediately to the right of the white mannequin inside the entrance area.
Multiple glass panels and glazed doors form the entrance face: at least three full-height glass panes/door sections are visible across the front elevation.

Three large rectangular brick-faced building windows are visible on the right-hand brick façade (two stacked vertically nearer the top right and one lower-right), though part of the façade extends beyond the image.
A translucent canopy/awning structure projects above the entrance, spanning the front elevation and supported by visible beams.
A wall-mounted sign or plaque with a green logo and text is visible to the left of the entrance interior (affixed to the glass or wall).
spatial_relations: The main entrance is centered in the mid-right of the image beneath a projecting translucent canopy; the entrance opens onto a small interior lobby area visible through full-height glass panels.

Perforated metal/cladding panels are mounted vertically at the building corner and along the front elevation, with two panels forming the near corner and additional panels flanking the glass entrance.

The white mannequin is positioned immediately inside the glass entrance area near the right side of the central bay, with a red rectangular/cube object directly to its right (from the viewer's perspective).

Silhouetted pedestrians appear on the external walkway to the left of the entrance and on the plaza in the foreground; one silhouette is shown walking through an interior doorway at the right side of the entrance lobby.
A brick-faced multi-storey façade rises above and behind the translucent canopy; windows in that brick façade are to the right of the entrance and align vertically.
colours_and_materials: The building exterior above the entrance is red brick (rectangular brick pattern).
Perforated panels and much of the entrance framing appear white or light grey metallic.
The canopy is translucent with white structural beams.
The ground plaza is laid with orange-brown herringbone-pattern paving (terracotta-colour bricks or tiles).
Glass is used extensively at the entrance (transparent/reflective panes) and interior walls are light-coloured (pale grey or off-white).
A red rectangular/cube object is visible inside the entrance near the mannequin.
uncertainties: The exact total count of human figures could be ambiguous due to ghosted/translucent silhouettes and partial occlusion; I report at least seven distinguishable figures but overlapping silhouettes may represent compositing rather than distinct people.

Small labels, logos and any fine-print text near the green logo plaque and on internal signage are partially legible; fragments beyond the transcribed phrases could not be clearly read from this image.
The identity or nature of the white human-form figures (mannequins vs. statues) cannot be confirmed from appearance alone.

The exact number of glass panes/door sections and perforated panels may extend beyond the visible crop; counts above reflect only clearly visible, individually distinguishable items within the image frame.
